title: Data in support of Inflammatory Profile of Glucocorticoid Responsive Polymyalgia Rheumatica Patients
projectDescription: Polymyalgia rheumatica (PMR) is a systemic inflammatory disorder with unknown etiology and overlapping symptoms with giant cell arthritis and rheumatoid arthritis (RA). The inflammatory pathogenesis in PMR remain poorly uncharacterized and biomarker studies very limited. The primary aim of this study was to thoroughly investigate the serum proteome and pro-/anti-inflammatory response during at debut and post-glucocorticoid treatment in comparison to DMARD-naïve RA patients, and healthy controls. Treatment naïve patients PMR patients were included and samples were obtained prior to treatment and after 3 months of treatment. Disease-modifying anti-rheumatic drug (DMARD) naïve RA patients with matched healthy controls were included for comparisons.
sampleProcessingProtocol: Preparation of serum samples were based on filter-aided sample preparation (FASP) for MS. Hence, 100µg total protein was dissolved in 5% sodium deoxycholate in 50mM triethylammonium bicarbonate (pH 8.6). Each sample was then reduced and alkylated using 10mM Tris(2-carboxyethyl)phosphine hydrochloride, and 25 mM chloroacetamide for 30 min at room temperature. The samples were then incubated overnight at 37°C with 1:100 (w/w) sequencing grade trypsin (Promega) per sample. The peptides were extracted by solvent phase transfer, and stored at -80°C until liquid chromatography tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) was performed. The individual serum samples were randomized and sequenced on a hybrid trapped ion mobility spectrometry (TIMS) quadrupole time of flight (QToF) mass spectrometer, i.e. TIMS-ToF Pro, (Bruker Daltonics, Bremen, Germany) coupled to modified nano-electrospray ion source (CaptiveSpray, Bruker Daltonics) with an applied voltage of 1800 V. Liquid chromatography was performed using a UltiMate 3000 UHPLC (Dionex, Thermo Scientific, Waltham, USA) setup. The peptide material was directly injected onto a C18 reversed phase column (IonOptics Aurora 25cm x 75µm, C18 1.6µm) kept at 50°C in a Sonation Column oven (Sonation GmbH, Biberach). Mobile phases A and B were 0.1% formic acid in HPLC grade water (v/v) and 0.1% formic acid in HPLC grade acetonitrile (v/v), respectively. The 85 min gradient had a flow 350nL/min and consisted the time windows: 0-25min at 2% B, 25-55min at 2-35% B, 55-60min at 35-95% B, 60-68min at 95% B, and 68-85min at 2%B. The TIMS-ToF Pro was operated in the default application TIMS-On and Parallel Accumulation - SErial Fragmentation (PASEF) positive mode. The applied RF fields for funnel 1 and 2 were set to 300 and 200 Vpp, respectively. Trapped ion mobility separation was performed via scanning a mobility range of 0.6 – 1.6 1/k0. All further experiments were acquired with a 100 ms ramp and 10 PASEF MS/MS scans per top10 with a cycle time of 1.32 sec. Signal-to-noise ratios was increased summation of individual TOF scans, and the target value was set to 20,000 a.u., and intensity threshold was set to 2,500 a.u. for all runs. The mass range for MS and MS/MS spectra were set to 100-1700 m/z.
dataProcessingProtocol: Mass spectrometry raw files were processed with MaxQuant (v 1.6.4.7) , using the Andromeda search engine and analyzed in Perseus. MaxQuant feature detection was set to TIMS half width 4, TIMS step 3, TIMS resolution 32,000, TIMS min ms/ms intensity 1.5, and TIMS collapse ms/ms on. Initial maximum tolerance was set to 70 ppm for precursors and 40 ppm for fragment ions. Following recalibration, precursor mass tolerance were set to less or equal to 20 ppm for, and a reverse decoy databased was used to enable a 1% false discovery rate for peptide spectrum matches. Label-free quantification was performed using the MaxQuant label-free-qauntification (MaxLFQ) algorithm. Proteins with statistically significant abundance change between treatments or disease groups were identified for each group using a permutation based two-sample t-tests between groups. For examples, polymyalgia patients before and after treatment were analyzed, using permutation based FDR with standard parameters (FDR=0.05, S0=1 and 250 randomizations).
